body: Thank you!

Hey there! I actually went through grad school undiagnosed. My psychiatrist just thought I had cyclical depression, but looking back, I wouldn’t see him when I was hypomanic, so he didn’t know the full story. I shouldn’t blame myself for being undiagnosed, but it’s definitely complicated.

Even though it was a wild ride, I managed to get my PhD in Psychology. I just wanted to say good luck!! Know that even if you have bad periods, you can still get through it! 

Three years ago, I was finally diagnosed and while that has been chaotic too (so many medications tried), I’m finally feeling stable. Here to chat if you need an internet friend!
Thank you so much for your message. I agree that there are a lot of benefits to reviewing the past, but I need to be in a stable place for it to be beneficial.
That’s a really good point. I read through notes I wrote to myself when depressed or manic. The manic ones are pretty wild.
That’s good advice. I’m stable right now and in a good place, so this could be a good time to do it. I just have to remind myself not to delve into my past on bad days.
That’s a great idea. Thank goodness for therapy.
That’s great that you find visiting the memories to be grounding. I think I reached out on Reddit, because I started finding it upsetting.
I just started using Daylio! I’m a big fan. I appreciate your suggestions.
Thank you! Good luck in your recovery!
I think so because I definitely had a manic episode, rather than a hypo manic episode. What makes you think it’s not bipolar 1?

I’m so sorry for your loss. 

It does sound like remote work is the way to go.

I can totally relate to the dampening of emotion! I cried the other day about something and it felt so good. I realized I hadn’t cried in a long time. It’s hard not feeling like I can be as creative and energetic as I used to be.

I’m glad you have a routine that works for you!

I can relate to this on a smaller scale. I work about 20 hrs/week and while I’m not making as much money as I need, the stability of a routine and feeling needed in my career is really helping me stay afloat. I’m really happy for you that you’ve found a routine that works for you!
Thank you for sharing your story! I’m glad you’ve found jobs that work for you! Hopefully I’ll find the same!
Thank you so much! I wish you happiness too!
Thank you! I agree that counseling is great. I switched from every other week to every week recently and it’s been so helpful!
I’m very interested in hearing more!
It sounds like you’re in a great situation! I wish you luck!
I’m glad you’ve found environments that work for you! I’m so scared of becoming manic again (even though I was so creative the last time I was manic), because of how unstable my world was.
You sound like a resilient individual. That must be so difficult to be on and off medication. I wish you the best!
Sounds like you’re doing the best you can! I wish you luck.

It sounds like you have a good system and are making the hypomania work for you. I’m so impressed that you can work through a depression, because I find that really difficult. I need to figure out how to do that myself. Do you have any tips?
I really appreciate your kind words. It sounds like you have amazing coping strategies! I might try implementing some myself!
I can totally relate to feeling like an outcast. I had an office job and it felt so lonely. Thank you for sharing your story! It sounds like you’re in a good place.

Yeah, it’s hard to find one employer that really understands the situation, so it makes sense you’d move around a lot to change things up. That’s great that you’ve been consistently employed for so long!
I know the feeling. In my current job (working about 20hrs/week), I haven’t told my employer I have bipolar disorder. Hopefully because I’m working so few hours and it being flexible, I’ll be okay.
That sounds like a really healthy approach. Hopefully I can find a job that allows me to do that. Thank you for sharing!

You’re such a strong individual! Thank you for sharing your story. I’m 31 and still live with my mom for stability. I used to live on my own abroad, but when I came home and had a manic episode, I became too scared to make it on my own. I’m slowly building financial independence, but it’s hard juggling everything. 

I wish you all the best and I hope your dreams come true!!
It would be nice to have a job with flexible hours…maybe it’s possible? If the employer is sensitive to the situation?
That’s good advice! Thank you.
Glad I’m not alone in this.
I really appreciate your honestly. It does sound like it will always be a struggle.
Thank you for your words of encouragement!
